ROL.thesis_one_line: A high-quality, recession-resistant pest-control roll-up, but management just admitted two straight quarters missed its own demand and margin expectations.
kill_criteria: Consolidated organic revenue growth below 5% for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026 was 5.7%; per company earnings releases, organic growth line).
GAAP operating margin down more than 100bps YoY for a third consecutive quarter (two already: Q1 -130bps, Q2 -110bps; per 8-K Ex-99.1 releases).
Net debt/EBITDA exceeding 1.5x (from ~0.5x currently; per 10-Q balance sheet + TTM operating income).
FCF/NI conversion below 80% for two consecutive quarters (TTM currently ~118%; per 10-Q cash-flow statement).
A second CFO or CEO departure within 12 months of Harkins' mid-2026 appointment (per Form 8-K Item 5.02 filings).
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 results explicitly missed management's own expectations on demand and margin (8-K Ex-99.1, 22-Jul-2026).
Two consecutive quarters of YoY GAAP operating-margin contraction (Q1 2026 -130bps, Q2 2026 -110bps).
New CFO (William Harkins) took office effective ~1-Jul-2026, concurrent with the demand/margin miss.
H1 2026 operating cash flow fell 9.7% YoY, partly on one-off tax-payment timing and a shift to semi-annual senior-note interest payments.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q09) framed the -38% 12-month momentum as likely 'sentiment-driven de-rating'; this diligence finds a real, management-acknowledged demand/margin miss in Q1-Q2 2026, not sentiment alone -- the triage's implicit bull case is only partly supported.
Triage's '48% Street upside' figure is an unsourced analyst-consensus claim (triage sources: general knowledge) not traced to any primary source in this diligence; not relied upon for the verdict.
ROL.confidence_in_thesis: medium - business quality and balance sheet are well evidenced, but the near-term demand/margin trend is genuinely unresolved until Q3 2026 confirms stabilization or continued deterioration

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for ROL (triage-advanced name, not in the top-70 V1 valuation set). The dossier's own reverse DCF (WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 3.25%) implies a 10-year FCF CAGR of ~5.8%, roughly in line with (not clearly below) an evidence-based base case of mid-single-digit-to-~7% growth once demand normalizes -- hence implied_vs_base = 'in_line' rather than 'below', and the verdict is WATCH rather than INCLUDE.

ROL.scenario_basis: TTM GAAP diluted EPS $1.10 (Q3'25-Q2'26); exit P/E 20x/25x/28x bear/base/bull on 2%/7%/11% 3-yr EPS CAGR; plus ~2.9% trailing dividend yield.

STE.thesis_one_line: The leading hospital-sterilization and infection-prevention company, growing across all three segments with FY2027 guidance reiterated and its big lawsuit overhang largely settled.
kill_criteria: Any subsequent quarterly update that lowers FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance below the current $11.10 floor (per 8-K Ex-99.1 releases).
AST segment constant-currency organic revenue growth below 3% for two consecutive quarters (Q1 FY27 was 5%; AST is the segment most exposed to device-maker capex cycles and EO-capacity regulation).
Net debt/EBITDA exceeding 2.0x (from ~0.7x currently; per 10-Q/10-K balance sheet and TTM operating income+D&A).
Total cash restructuring costs for the NC Center of Excellence exceeding $60m (25% above the high end of the disclosed $40-50m cash-cost range).
A new, unresolved ethylene-oxide trial verdict or judgment against a STERIS subsidiary in a jurisdiction other than the currently-settled Illinois matters.
key_adverse_facts: Q1 FY2027 operating cash flow fell 12.6% YoY on a working-capital swing (8-K Ex-99.1, 5-Aug-2026).
FY2027 capex guidance raised to ~$450m (from $375m) and FCF guidance cut to ~$800m (from $850m) to fund a new manufacturing-consolidation restructuring (Item 2.05, 8-K filed 2026-08-05).

New restructuring plan (~$55-70m pre-tax charges through fiscal 2030) closing plants in St. Louis, MO and Plymouth, MN, concurrent with a separate ~$60m Mentor, OH plant investment -- two overlapping manufacturing transitions.

Ethylene-oxide personal-injury litigation was a multi-year overhang; settlement dates (Mar-2025, Oct-2025) sourced from secondary summaries, not independently re-verified against the primary legal-proceedings note at Standard depth.
data_conflicts: Triage's '26% street upside' figure is an unsourced analyst-consensus claim (triage sources: general knowledge of Steris sterilization moat) not traced to a primary source in this diligence; not relied upon for the verdict.
Triage described organic growth as 'mid-single-digit'; FY2026 actual reported revenue growth was high-single-digit (+8.7%) with margin expansion, i.e. better than the triage's own characterization.
STE.confidence_in_thesis: high - broad-based, multi-segment growth with guidance reiterated and a major litigation overhang substantially settled; the main reservation is valuation fullness, not evidence quality

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for STE (triage-advanced name, not in the top-70 V1 valuation set). The dossier's own reverse DCF (WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 3.25%) implies a 10-year FCF CAGR of ~4.8%, below an evidence-based base case of ~7-9% anchored to management's own FY2027 guidance (adjusted EPS +9-11%, revenue +7-8%) moderating over time -- hence implied_vs_base = 'below' and the verdict is INCLUDE.

STE.scenario_basis: TTM adjusted diluted EPS $10.42 (FY26 $10.17 - Q1FY26 $2.34 + Q1FY27 $2.59); exit adj. P/E 17x/20x/22x bear/base/bull on 5%/9%/12% 3-yr EPS CAGR; plus ~1.2% trailing dividend yield.

USB.thesis_one_line: A diversified super-regional bank with payments and wealth scale, priced like it can't grow despite five straight quarters of improving margins and credit quality.
kill_criteria: Basel III standardized CET1 ratio falling below 9.5% (from 10.8% currently; per quarterly earnings releases / 10-Q regulatory-capital disclosures, consolidated).
Net charge-off ratio rising above 0.75% for two consecutive quarters (from 0.53% currently; per earnings releases, consolidated).
Efficiency ratio rising back above 60% for two consecutive quarters (from 57.1% currently; per earnings releases, consolidated, non-GAAP as defined by the company).
Net interest margin compressing more than 15 bps YoY in any single quarter (currently +13 bps YoY; per earnings releases, taxable-equivalent basis, consolidated).
A new material regulatory enforcement action (CFPB, OCC or Federal Reserve) carrying a fine or consent order exceeding $50m.
key_adverse_facts: Average loan growth (+7.1% YoY, Q2 2026) is outpacing average deposit growth (+2.4% YoY), a funding-cost risk if the gap widens.

Two CFPB consent orders (sham accounts, $37.5m penalty; ReliaCard/COVID unemployment-benefit freezes, $20.7m penalty) were only terminated by the regulator in Aug/Sep 2025 -- a recent history of consumer-compliance enforcement, now formally closed.
BTIG (Condor Trading LP) acquisition closed 1-Jun-2026; only one partial quarter of results exists, so integration and full-cycle profitability are unproven.

The b1 quant feed's ROE field (12.11%, percentile 0.311) understates USB's own-reported profitability (14.0% return on average common equity, 18.7% ROTCE, Q2 2026) -- a data-conflict, not an adverse fact about the business.
data_conflicts: Triage's ROE figure (12.6%) matches USB's own Q1 2026 return on average common equity exactly, but is now stale: Q2 2026 ROE improved to 14.0% (ROTCE 18.7%). The b1 quant feed's separate 'roe' field (12.11%) is a different, XBRL-derived proxy and does not match either the triage figure or the company's own reported ratio -- three different 'ROE' numbers exist across sources for the same company, and they must not be treated as interchangeable.
USB.confidence_in_thesis: high - multi-quarter, cross-metric improving trend (NIM, efficiency, ROTCE, credit quality) corroborated by the company's own reconciled disclosures and confirmed against its medium-term target framework

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for USB (top-70 name but bank valuation requires the sector-specific P/TBV method, not V1's generic approach; not in the V1 table). Gordon-growth-on-ROTCE (P/TBV = 1 + (ROTCE-r)/(r-g)) implies the current 1.98x P/TBV prices in only ~0-2% long-run growth at a 9.5-10% cost of equity, well below an evidence-based base case of ~6-9% tangible-book growth capacity given high-teens ROTCE and ~50% earnings retention -- hence implied_vs_base = 'below' and the verdict is INCLUDE.

USB.scenario_basis: Tangible book value/share $30.04 (Q2 2026); exit P/TBV 1.55x/2.00x/2.30x bear/base/bull on 5%/8%/11% 3-yr TBV-per-share CAGR; plus ~3.5% trailing dividend yield.
